key_insight: A symmetry-aware variational framework can simulate the finite-size Dicke model on both digital qubit devices and hybrid qubit-boson platforms, while recovering the model’s critical behavior in the large-spin limit.
engineering_relevance: The approach points to a more resource-efficient path for near-term quantum hardware to model collective light-matter systems and broader spin-boson physics.
method: Variationally encode the finite-size Dicke model for fully qubit-based digital simulation.
Develop a hybrid qubit-boson ansatz that leverages the bosonic mode directly to reduce quantum resources.
Test the framework on classical emulators and trapped-ion quantum computers.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model reproduces the Dicke model’s characteristic critical behavior in the appropriate large-spin limit and can be implemented on emulators and trapped-ion hardware.
watch_item: Performance on current trapped-ion hardware is somewhat limited by noise, which may constrain accuracy and scalability.
paper_title: Simulating the Dicke Model on Qubit-Based and hybrid Qubit-Boson-Based Quantum Computers
